evidence_quote: Every sample in this compendium is described by the authors as 'Pst-infected': the cohort exists because the plants were showing yellow rust, collected under an explicit surveillance programme ('field pathogenomics', ev-ada21-surveillance). The sampling therefore conditioned on disease. This is the strongest available test of the cryptic co-infection hypothesis, because the authors reported Pst and only Pst, so any further pathogen in the reads is unreported by construction. It is simultaneously unusable as a prevalence denominator, for the same reason. Lab rows are marked 'inoculated' rather than 'disease-selected': there an archived isolate was deliberately applied to wheat, so disease is present by the experimenter's design, not by the sampler's choice.

Columns: Sample ID, Collection date, Country, Location, Wheat variety, Data reference, Accession number, then alignment statistics. Every 'This study' row carries a town: Louville-la-Chenard, Adisham, Dereham, Mersea, Otley, Newton, Whittlesford, Glenrothes, Hemmingen, Melton Mowbray, Headley Hall, Ickleton, Newark, Fowlmere, Allonnes, Layerdelahaye, West Wickham, Chelsworth, Bohl-Iggelheim. The sheet has one key error: ERS4270296 appears on both 15.0040 (Cambridge) and 15.0130 (Whattisham) while ERS4270297, which ENA does hold, appears on none. Rows are otherwise in strict ascending accession order, so the intended mapping is almost certainly 296 then 297, but that is an inference about a typo and the two towns are 50 km apart, so corredor21.py drops both rather than guessing.
